topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): add agreement interop validation strategy
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds an additive `agreement` interop-validation strategy to proxyd. It fans each `checkAccessList` out to all configured supervisor urls concurrently and combines the verdicts by quorum agreement.

- A definitive verdict is valid, or **any** filter JSON-RPC rejection: the supervisor verdict codes (`-3204xx..-3215xx`) *and* the generic invalid-params code (`-32602`, e.g. a malformed/fabricated access list — "failed to parse access entry"). `ParseInteropError` reads the filter's actual JSON-RPC code (including for JSON-RPC errors returned over HTTP 200, which are `rpc.Error` not `rpc.HTTPError`), so rejections are identified by code, not message. Non-verdicts that do not count: failsafe (handled separately), JSON-RPC internal (`-32603`/`-32000`), cancellation (`499`), and transport/5xx.
- **Fast-accept at the minimum:** the strategy decides as soon as `min_responses` definitive verdicts arrive and never awaits slow or unresponded endpoints.
- **Failsafe takes priority among received verdicts:** if any *received* response reports failsafe enabled (dedicated code `-320602`), the message is rejected, even when the minimum accepts are also in hand. A failsafe verdict short-circuits the fan-out; before returning an accept the strategy does a non-blocking drain of already-buffered verdicts so a failsafe that has already arrived beats a met quorum. It never blocks on an endpoint that has not yet responded.
- All-valid (with at least `min_responses` definitive verdicts) accepts; all-invalid rejects with the real error (e.g. a `-32602` parse rejection from every endpoint yields a clean reject, not quorum-not-reached); a mix logs and rejects; fewer than `min_responses` fails closed. Disagreement detection is best-effort (consistent with fast-accept).
- `min_responses` defaults to `len(urls)` (unanimity) and is validated to `1..len(urls)` in `Start`.
- Existing first-supervisor / multicall / health-aware strategies and `performCheckAccessListOp` are unchanged.

Selected via `[interop_validation] strategy = "agreement"` + `min_responses`. Single-endpoint configs are equivalent to today (min defaults to 1).

**Hard cutover:** failsafe detection keys on the dedicated RPC code `-320602` (`ParseInteropError` routes it independently of message/HTTP status). This relies on op-interop-filter emitting `-320602` — a prerequisite server PR — so filters must deploy that change before this lands.

This is the proxyd half of a multi-repo change; the op-reth mempool half ships separately.

Test plan: `interop_strategy_test.go` unit tests (failsafe hard-reject by code, failsafe-priority-over-met-quorum, slow non-failsafe endpoint does not delay accept, failsafe short-circuits a slow backend, generic `-32602` parse rejection counts as a definitive invalid, verdict-classification coverage) plus `TestInteropValidation_AgreementStrategy` and config tests in `integration_tests/interop_validation_test.go`. Agreement + failsafe tests pass under `-race -count=20`. `gofmt -l .` and `golangci-lint run ./...` are clean; the interop package and interop integration tests pass under `-race`. Several unrelated, timing-sensitive integration tests (`TestMulticall`, `TestWSClientExceedReadLimit`, `TestFrontendMaxRPSLimit`, `TestMaxConcurrentRPCs`) flake under the race detector and reproduce unchanged on `main`.

topPRs.title: chore(deps): bump github.com/quic-go/quic-go from 0.39.4 to 0.57.0 in /peer-mgmt-service
topPRs.author: dependabot
topPRs.body:
Bumps [github.com/quic-go/quic-go](https://github.com/quic-go/quic-go) from 0.39.4 to 0.57.0.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/quic-go/quic-go's releases.

v0.57.0

This release contains a fix for CVE-2025-64702 by reworking the HTTP/3 header processing logic:

  • Both client and server now send their respective header size constraints using the SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE setting: #5431
  • For any QPACK-related errors, the correct error code (QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED) is now used: #5439
  • QPACK header parsing is now incremental (instead of parsing all headers at once), which is ~5-10% faster and reduces allocations: #5435 (and quic-go/qpack#67)
  • The server now sends a 431 status code (Request Header Fields Too Large) when encountering HTTP header fields exceeding the size constraint: #5452

 

Breaking Changes

  • http3: Transport.MaxResponseBytes is now an int (before: int64): #5433  

Notable Fixes

  • qlogwriter: fix storing of event schemas (this prevented qlog event logging from working for HTTP/3): #5430
  • http3: errors sending the request are now ignored, instead, the response from the server is read (thereby allowing the client to read the status code, for example): #5432

What's Changed

  • build(deps): bump golangci/golangci-lint-action from 8 to 9 by @​dependabot[bot] in quic-go/quic-go#5426
  • qlogwriter: fix storing of event schemas by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5430
  • http3: send SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE in the SETTINGS frame by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5431
  • http3: read response after encountering error sending the request by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5432
  • http3: make Transport.MaxResponseBytes an int by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5433
  • http3: add a benchmark for header parsing by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5435
  • update qpack to v0.6.0 by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5434
  • http3: use QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED for QPACK errors by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5439
  • add documentation for Conn.NextConnection by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5442
  • ackhandler: don’t generate an immediate ACK for the first packet by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5447
  • don’t arm connection timer for connection ID retirement by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5449
  • README: add nodepass to list of projects by @​yosebyte in quic-go/quic-go#5448
  • qlogwriter: use synctest to make tests deterministic by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5454
  • http3: limit size of decompressed headers by @​marten-seemann in quic-go/quic-go#5452

New Contributors

  • @​yosebyte made their first contribution in quic-go/quic-go#5448

Full Changelog: https://github.com/quic-go/quic-go/compare/v0.56.0...v0.57.0

v0.56.0

This release introduces qlog support for HTTP/3 (#5367, #5372, #5374, #5375, #5376, #5381, #5383).

For this, we completely changed how connection tracing works. Instead of a general-purpose logging.ConnectionTracer (which we removed entirely), we now have a qlog-specific tracer (#5356, #5417). quic-go users can now implement their own qlog events.

It also removes the Prometheus-based metrics collection. Please comment on the tracking issue (#5294) if you rely on metrics and are interested in seeing metrics brought back in a future release.

Notable Changes

  • replaced the unmaintained gojay with a custom, performance-optimized JSON encoder (#5353, #5371)

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 5b2d212 http3: limit size of decompressed headers (#5452)
  • e80b378 qlogwriter: use synctest to make tests deterministic (#5454)
  • d43c589 README: add nodepass to list of projects (#5448)
  • ca2835d don’t arm connection timer for connection ID retirement (#5449)
  • e84ebae ackhandler: don’t generate an immediate ACK for the first packet (#5447)
  • d4d168f add documentation for Conn.NextConnection (#5442)
  • 4cdebbe http3: use QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED for QPACK errors (#5439)
  • b7886d5 update qpack to v0.6.0 (#5434)
  • 2fc9705 http3: add a benchmark for header parsing (#5435)
  • dafdd6f http3: make Transport.MaxResponseBytes an int (#5433)

topPRs.author: dependabot
topPRs.body:
Bumps [github.com/quic-go/quic-go](https://github.com/quic-go/quic-go) from 0.39.4 to 0.59.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/quic-go/quic-go's releases.

v0.59.1

This patch release backports quic-go/quic-go#5642, which adds validation for HTTP/3 trailers.

v0.59.0

This release adds a couple of new features:

  • Adds an API to peek stream data on ReceiveStream and Stream: #5501
  • Adds an API to peek the next varint on a stream: #5502
  • Reworks the API exposed by the HTTP/3 package for WebTransport: #5509, #5512. Regular HTTP/3 use cases should not be affected by these changes.
  • Adds support for HTTP request trailers (trailers sent by the client): #5507

Breaking Changes

  • Removes the deprecated ClientHelloInfo: #5497
  • Removes the deprecated ConnectionTracingID and ConnectionTracingKey: #5521
  • http3: the qlogger is now closed after all streams have been handled: #5524
  • The ConnectionState now reports both the local and the remote status of the QUIC Datagram and Reliable Stream Reset extensions: #5533

Other Notable Fixes

  • Fixes an infinite loop of PING-only packets caused by a bug in the PTO queueing logic: #5538 and #5539
  • http3: Fixes a race condition between new request streams and GOAWAY: #5522
  • qlog: Fixes a race condition between RecordEvent and Close: #5523

topPRs.title: docs(op-conductor-ops): update README for installable package layout
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`op-conductor-ops` was converted to an installable Python package with a poetry script entry point in #638, but the README still documents the old invocation. This updates the setup/usage docs to match.

### What was stale
- Referenced the removed `./op-conductor-ops` wrapper script
- Claimed it "calls `poetry run python main.py`" — `main.py` never existed in the new layout
- A broken/duplicated PATH export: `export PATH="export PATH="...""`

### Changes
- Setup now points at `poetry install` registering the `op-conductor-ops` console script
- Usage and examples use `poetry run op-conductor-ops ...`
- Removed the broken PATH line; kept the `CONDUCTOR_CONFIG` export

## Test plan
- `poetry install` + `poetry run op-conductor-ops --help` renders the CLI help as documented
